Pros:
Hardness over HRC60 — minimal wear with abrasive filaments (carbon fiber, steel, wood, boron carbide, tungsten, phosphorescent)
Rated to 450°C — handles PEEK, PA6, PA12 and other engineering plastics
Burr-free tip and inner hole roughness under Ra0.4 for smooth extrusion
Minimum hole diameter 0.1mm / ±0.01mm for high accuracy
Cons:
Lower thermal conductivity than brass/copper — may need +5-15°C vs brass profiles
Not the cheapest hardened steel V6 option (clones run ~$3-5)
0.2mm and 0.4mm currently out of stock at Fabreeko
Name: V6 Hardened Steel
Description: Phaetus's hardened steel V6-style nozzle, made from imported die steel with hardness over HRC60 for printing abrasive composites (carbon fiber, steel, wood, boron carbide, tungsten, phosphorescent pigment) as well as conventional materials. Temperature resistance up to 450°C covers PEEK, PA6 and PA12. The tip is burr-free with inner hole roughness under Ra0.4, and the minimum hole diameter of 0.1mm (±0.01mm) allows highly accurate printing. Standard M6 V6 thread — drop-in for V6, Dragon, Rapido and other V6-compatible hotends. Available in 0.2, 0.4, 0.6 and 0.8mm.
Verdict Label: Abrasion-resistant V6 nozzle for composites at a fair price

Pros:
One-handed nozzle changes via the XG's three-point mounting — no tools, no hot-tightening routine
Hardened steel variant is abrasive-safe and costs only $12.99
Cheap spares: brass from $5.99
Fits the XG's Creality and E3D V6 style groove mounts via the hotend itself
Cons:
XG hotend only — this nozzle fits nothing else
Almost no published specifications (Fabreeko: 'More info coming soon'; no max-temp or thread figure anywhere)
User report: could not push filament much faster than ~15 mm³/s — not really an upgrade over stock
Record is ambiguous: one listing covers Brass, Hardened Steel and Copper at different prices (see held list)
Name: DropEffect XG
Description: DropEffect (Phaetus) replacement nozzle for the XG hotend, Phaetus's sub-brand hotend with an extreme temperature gradient and one-handed nozzle changes via three-point mounting between the ring heater block and the frame. The XG heats to 300°C. Fabreeko sells the nozzle in Brass ($5.99), Hardened Steel ($12.99) and Copper ($12.99), all in 0.2, 0.4, 0.6 and 0.8mm; the XG ships with a hardened steel and a brass 0.4mm nozzle. Documentation is thin — Fabreeko lists 'More info coming soon' and no thread or max-temp figure is published — and one user reports a ~15 mm³/s flow ceiling, so treat this as a spare for XG owners rather than an upgrade. NOTE: this single record spans three materials at two prices; it likely needs splitting into three records or a decision that it represents the hardened steel variant.
Verdict Label: Spare nozzle for the DropEffect XG — XG owners only

Pros: Rated to 500°C for high-temperature filaments; copper body and spreader for efficient heat transmission; Chromium Nitride coating for corrosion prevention and non-stick behaviour; tool-free cold swapping with no hot tightening; grey colour with engraved size markings
Cons: Capped at 300°C unless paired with a High Temperature Hotside kit; copper is soft and not abrasion-resistant — not for fibre-filled filaments; no silicone socks included
Name: Revo High Temperature
Description: Copper Revo nozzle with a copper spreader and Chromium Nitride coating for corrosion prevention and non-stick properties, rated to 500°C for high-temperature printing. Preassembled nozzle and HeatBreak in one unit for tool-free cold swapping. Needs a Revo High Temperature Hotside kit to actually reach 500°C — with a 40W or 60W HeaterCore it is temperature-limited to 300°C. Copper construction, so not intended for abrasive filaments (see HTA/ObXidian for those).
Verdict Label: Copper high-temperature nozzle for 500°C printing without abrasives

Pros:
CHT geometry splits filament into 3 strands for market-leading volumetric flow on non-abrasive materials
Nickel-coated copper — superior heat conduction and thermal performance
FIN standard geometry interlocks with the silicone boot, fully insulating the hotend
6mm hex for easy interchangeability; 1.5 Nm torque spec with Slice torque wrench

Non-abrasive filaments only — coated copper, not hardened; use GammaMaster FIN for CF/GF
Mako/FIN only — standard M6 V6 nozzles will not fit, and this will not fit a V6 block
Torque-sensitive: do not exceed 1.5 Nm
0.2mm size listed by Bondtech but not stocked at Fabreeko
Name: CHT Mako
Description: Bondtech's coated-copper CHT nozzle in the FIN (Free and open-source Insulated Nozzle) standard, made for the Slice Engineering Mako hotend on Bambu Lab X1/X1C/X1E/P1P/P1S printers. The FIN geometry interlocks with the silicone boot to fully insulate the hotend, and the CHT inlet pattern splits filament into three strands for market-leading volumetric flow with rigid non-abrasive materials. Nickel-coated copper gives superior heat conduction; working temperature up to 450°C per Bondtech's datasheet (the Mako hotend and Bambu firmware cap it lower in practice). 6mm hex, M5x0.8 FIN thread — not M6, so it fits the Mako only. Available in 0.2, 0.4, 0.6 and 0.8mm.
Verdict Label: High-flow CHT nozzle for the Slice Mako (FIN)

Pros: At least 5x the wear resistance of ObXidian; prints any filament including glow in the dark; rated to 500°C; non-stick coating prevents build-up and reduces print crashes; improved thermal performance for stronger interlayer adhesion; tool-free cold swapping with no hot tightening
Cons: Premium price; no silicone socks included or recommended above 300°C; exotic filled materials (e.g. Polymaker Fiberon range) can still cause wear over time; filled materials can jam the smaller 0.4mm orifice — check filament datasheets; 500°C needs a capable hotend/heater, not just the nozzle
Name: Revo ObXidian 500
Description: E3D's premium abrasive Revo nozzle, powered by ObXiDian 500 technology: at least five times more wear resistant than the standard ObXidian, so most abrasive materials — including UV-reactive glow-in-the-dark filaments — simply won't wear it. Low surface-energy coating prevents plastic build-up for pristine prints and fewer crashes, and optimised thermal performance improves interlayer adhesion. Rated to 500°C (no silicone socks supplied, as silicone is only rated to 300°C). Preassembled nozzle and HeatBreak in one unit for tool-free cold swapping.
Verdict Label: Five times the wear resistance of ObXidian, rated to 500°C

Pros:
Original CHT design — patented EP3445568A1 / US11712847B2, precise machining
Nickel coating resists corrosion and plastic adhesion
Widest size range of any CHT nozzle (0.25–1.8mm)
5-pack available at volume discount
Cons:
5× the price of AliExpress clones with identical flow performance
Not abrasive-safe — nickel coating is not hardened
Requires 6mm wrench (standard)
Name: CHT
Description: The original Bondtech CHT (Core Heating Technology) nozzle, manufactured by Bondtech AB under their EP3445568A1 / US11712847B2 patents. The CHT design splits filament into 3 strands via multiple bore holes, increasing heating wall surface area and enabling 25–35% higher volumetric flow vs standard nozzles (CNCKitchen validated). The Bondtech version adds a nickel coating for corrosion resistance and reduced plastic adhesion. Fits standard M6×1×7.5×12.5 RepRap spec heat blocks — compatible with E3D V6, Dragon, Rapido, Mosquito, Copperhead, and all M6 variants. The $5 Mellow/Trianglelab clones deliver the same flow results if budget is a priority.
Verdict Label: The original CHT — patented, precise machining, widest size range

Pros:
German-made by Brozzl GmbH with tight manufacturing tolerances (±0.01mm concentricity ≤0.02mm)
Ruby tip: high hardness, non-stick surface, excellent for abrasive filaments
Inner hole roughness ≤Ra0.4, ruby hole roughness ≤Ra0.012 — precision-machined
V6 (M6) and MK8 threading available
Cons:
Price not listed on site — sold exclusively through European resellers
Harder to source in North America vs. Ruby tips from E3D or other brands
Ruby has lower thermal conductivity than brass — may need temperature adjustment
Name: Ruby
Description: Brozzl GmbH is a German manufacturer of precision 3D printer nozzles. Their Ruby Nozzle combines a brass body with a synthetic ruby gemstone insert at the tip, providing extreme hardness for abrasive filament resistance alongside a naturally smooth, non-stick surface. Manufactured to tighter tolerances than most competitors: ±0.01mm orifice tolerance, concentricity ≤0.02mm, inner hole roughness ≤Ra0.4. Available in V6 (M6) and MK8 threading in multiple diameters. Pricing not listed on website — sold through European resellers. Can be found via 3DJake, Amazon.de, and similar.
Verdict Label: European quality ruby

Pros:
25–35% flow rate improvement over standard brass at 0.6mm+ (CNCKitchen validated)
~$5 vs $25 for original Bondtech CHT
Standard M6 thread — fits any V6-compatible block
Cons:
Not abrasive-safe (brass wears quickly with CF/GF)
Quality varies by vendor batch
Clone status — no official documentation
Name: CHT Brass
Description: Third-party implementation of Bondtech's CHT (Core Heating Technology) design, sold under brands like Mellow3D and Trianglelab on AliExpress. The CHT design splits filament into 3 strands through multiple bores to dramatically increase surface contact with the heater block walls. CNCKitchen testing consistently shows 25–35% higher volumetric flow compared to standard brass at 0.6mm and above. The M6 clones are effectively identical to the original Bondtech CHT at a fraction of the price and are the default nozzle recommendation for Voron builders wanting more speed without switching to hardened steel.
Verdict Label: Best bang-for-buck high-flow upgrade

Pros:
Higher volumetric flow than standard Revo
Tool-free hot-swap retained
Good for speed printing with 0.6mm+
Cons:
Not available in 0.25mm (fine detail)
Pricier than standard Revo
Still not abrasive-safe
Name: Revo High Flow
Description: The Revo High Flow nozzle uses E3D's multi-bore high-flow geometry to increase volumetric throughput over the standard Revo nozzle. Designed for users who want faster print speeds without leaving the Revo ecosystem. Available in 0.4, 0.6, and 0.8mm. Retains the tool-free quick-swap mounting. Not to be confused with the ObXidian HF, which is also abrasive-safe.
Verdict Label: Revo speed upgrade for high-throughput printing

Pros:
Proprietary hardened alloy with 2.7x better thermal conductivity vs standard hardened steel
Low Gamma anti-adhesive coating rated to 380°C — non-PTFE, no temp ceiling for most materials
Limited Lifetime Warranty against abrasive wear
Multiple geometries: RepRap (V6), AP3X (belt/non-planar), Vase (large format), FIN (insulated)
Rockwell C63 hardness

Engraved orifice size on three sides

Name: GammaMaster
Description: The GammaMaster is Slice Engineering's flagship nozzle, made from a proprietary hardened alloy that achieves 2.7x the thermal conductivity of standard hardened steel — meaning no need to raise nozzle temperatures when printing abrasive filaments. Features their Low Gamma anti-adhesive surface coating (rated to 380°C) to prevent plastic buildup at the tip. Available in four geometries: RepRap (standard V6, M6 threading), AP3X (2mm longer tip for belt printers and non-planar printing), Vase (large-format vase mode), and FIN (insulated nozzle standard, Mako hotend only). Orifice sizes from 0.2mm to 1.8mm (plus 2.4mm Vase). Carries a Limited Lifetime Warranty against abrasive wear. Sold direct by Slice Engineering.
Verdict Label: Best thermal/abrasive balance

Vanadium tool steel — excellent hardness and wear resistance for abrasive filaments
Better thermal conductivity than standard hardened steel
Currently on sale at $30.61 (from $43.74)

Vanadium steel properties still being evaluated by community vs. alternatives

Vanadium steel offers abrasion resistance comparable to hardened steel with potentially better thermal properties. Less common in the 3D printing nozzle market than hardened steel or bimetal alternatives. Sold directly by Bondtech. Currently listed on sale.
Verdict Label: Less common but capable

Pros:
Solid polycrystalline diamond tip — virtually permanent wear resistance against any filament, abrasive or not
Best-in-class thermal conductivity; generally runs at lower temperatures than other nozzles
Prints any filament from PLA/ABS to abrasive carbon fibers with one nozzle — no more nozzle changes
Easy to clean, reduces tip clogging; great for ironing
Made in USA; 30-Day Performance Promise

FIN geometry with 6mm hex, torqued to 1.5 Nm on the Mako. Made in the USA with a 30-Day Performance Promise. Available in 0.4, 0.6 and 0.8mm.

ALPHA positions it as the performance-value option — excellent abrasion resistance and strong thermal performance without stepping up to polycrystalline diamond. Sold in 0.4 and 0.6mm for V6, Qidi Plus 4 and Prusa Nextruder.

Name: Revo ObXidian

Preassembled nozzle and HeatBreak in one unit for tool-free cold swapping, with colour-coded socks and engraved size markings.

No 0.2mm or fine-detail size offered
Name: V6 Plated Copper
Description: Phaetus's copper plated (nickel-plated copper alloy) V6-style nozzle. The copper alloy body offers thermal conductivity of 330 W/m·K for even tip temperature and stable extrusion, and the nozzle is rated to 500°C — the best choice in this line for PEEK, PEKK, PEI, PSU, PPSU and other filaments that melt above 300°C, which an ordinary brass nozzle cannot handle. The nickel plating and sub-Ra0.4 bore give a smooth, low-adhesion surface. Standard M6 V6 thread. Available in 0.25, 0.4, 0.6 and 0.8mm. Not abrasive-safe: this is a high-temperature nozzle for non-filled filaments.
Verdict Label: Budget high-temperature V6 nozzle — copper core, 500°C rated

Pros: Rated to 500°C for high-temperature engineering filaments; hardened steel tip plus Chromium Nitride coating for strong abrasion and corrosion resistance; copper carrier/spreader for good heat transmission; non-stick coating reduces plastic build-up; tool-free cold swapping with no hot tightening
Cons: Capped at 300°C unless paired with a High Temperature Hotside kit; aggressive filled materials (e.g. Polymaker PolyMide range) can still wear it over time; no silicone socks included; not everlasting under extreme material conditions
Name: Revo HTA
Description: High-temperature, abrasive-resistant Revo nozzle: a hardened steel tip on a copper carrier with a copper spreader segment, coated in Chromium Nitride for extra abrasive resistance, corrosion prevention and non-stick properties, rated to 500°C. Preassembled nozzle and HeatBreak in one unit for tool-free cold swapping. Needs a Revo High Temperature Hotside kit to actually reach 500°C — with a 40W or 60W HeaterCore it is temperature-limited to 300°C.
Verdict Label: High-temperature abrasive nozzle for engineering filaments up to 500°C

Pros:
Teflon/PTFE exterior sleeve prevents PETG and sticky filaments from adhering to nozzle tip
Significantly reduces stringing and blobbing on PETG
Available in Brass, Plated Copper, and Hardened Steel base materials
Budget-friendly at $8.49
Cons:
Hard 280°C max — PTFE coating degrades and off-gases above this temperature
Not suitable for high-temp materials (ASA, PC, PA)
Not abrasion resistant — PTFE exterior is soft
Name: PlastiGlide
Description: Fabreeko's PlastiGlide is a V6-style nozzle with a PTFE/Teflon exterior sleeve around the tip zone. The coating prevents PETG, sticky PLA, and similar materials from adhering to the outside of the nozzle, dramatically reducing blobbing, oozing, and stringing. Max temp is 280°C — the PTFE limits high-temperature use. Available in Brass, Plated Copper, and Hardened Steel core materials. V6 threading (M6 x 1.0), 0.4mm and 0.6mm orifice sizes.
Verdict Label: PETG anti-stick specialist

Pros:
Phaetus's proprietary EndCoat™ DLC-inspired surface coating provides anti-adhesive properties
Lowest price entry into coated abrasive nozzles at ~$9
Available for multiple printer platforms
Cons:
EndCoat™ coating longevity under sustained abrasive use is less proven than uncoated HS or SiC
Limited community testing data vs. more established options
Coating may degrade with very aggressive filaments (high SiC or metal-fill)
Name: EndCoat
Description: Phaetus's EndCoat™ nozzle uses their proprietary diamond-like carbon (DLC) inspired coating applied to a hardened steel substrate. The coating reduces surface energy for anti-adhesion at the nozzle tip while maintaining the abrasion resistance of the hardened steel base. Entry-level coated nozzle option at ~$9. Available for Rapido/Dragon (M6), and multiple printer-specific platforms. Multiple variants in the Phaetus catalog (EndCoat K2 Series at $12.90, EndCoat Creality at $12.90, etc.).
Verdict Label: Budget DLC-coated option

Pros:
Diamond-reinforced filament channel + PCD tip: extreme wear resistance with near-brass extrusion stability (Fraunhofer tested)
Very high thermal conductivity for a wear-resistant nozzle — no temperature penalty like steel or ruby
Lifetime guarantee from the manufacturer
Made by Gühring, an established precision cutting-tool maker
Cons:
$214.99 — by far the most expensive nozzle in the database, ~3x a ruby nozzle
Only 3 diameters (0.4/0.6/0.8)
Overkill for non-abrasive printing; a brass or coated nozzle is cheaper and just as good for PLA/PETG
Name: DIANOZ Pro
Description: The DIANOZ Pro is an industrial-grade diamond nozzle made by German precision cutting-tool leader Gühring and sold by Slice Engineering. It combines a stainless steel body with a polycrystalline diamond (PCD) tip and a diamond-reinforced filament channel, giving extreme wear resistance with the stable, brass-like extrusion behaviour Fraunhofer testing confirmed — more uniform than ruby nozzles across temperature and speed ranges. Substrate temperature rating 550°C, 6.1mm hex, RepRap geometry, lifetime guarantee. Available in 0.4, 0.6 and 0.8mm.
Verdict Label: Industrial diamond nozzle — extreme wear resistance at an extreme price

Pros:
Tool-free hot-swap at temperature
Wide diameter range (0.15mm to 1.0mm)
No nozzle-block thread stripping risk
Accurate, machined brass for PLA/PETG/ABS
Cons:
Proprietary system — only works with Revo hotends
Not abrasive-safe (brass wears with CF/GF)
Premium price per nozzle vs generic M6
Name: Revo Brass
Description: E3D's RapidChange Revo nozzle attaches directly to the heater core rather than threading into a heater block. The tool-free hot-swap system lets you change diameters in seconds while the hotend is at temp — no wrenches, no stripped threads. The entry-level option in the Revo nozzle lineup, these standard brass nozzles cover PLA, PETG, ASA, and ABS with diameters spanning 0.15mm to 1.0mm. For abrasive filaments, step up to the Revo ObXidian or HTA variants.
Verdict Label: The easiest nozzle upgrade: hot-swap in seconds, no tools

Pros:
True PCD insert — not a coating, permanent abrasion resistance
Exceptional thermal conductivity vs. hardened steel
Made in USA by an industrial diamond tooling manufacturer
Multiple platform variants available (Bambu, Nextruder, Revo, K2, MK8)
Cons:
Very high price point — premium over all other abrasive-safe options
Overkill for occasional CF/GF use
Limited diameter selection vs. standard nozzle lines
Name: DiamondBack V6
Description: DiamondBack Nozzles is a brand of US Synthetic Corporation (Orem, Utah), a manufacturer of polycrystalline diamond (PCD) industrial cutting tools. Their 3D printer nozzles use a solid PCD insert — not a coating — providing virtually permanent wear resistance against abrasive filaments. E3D carries DiamondBack as an authorized distribution partner; DiamondBack also sells direct at diamondbacknozzles.com. The V6-compatible version fits standard E3D V6, Dragon, and Rapido hotends with M6 threading. Additional platform variants available for Bambu Lab, Prusa Nextruder, Revo, and Creality K2.
Verdict Label: Industrial-grade PCD tip — extreme wear resistance at extreme cost

Pros:
Stainless steel is durable and corrosion-resistant
Lead-free — suitable for food-grade and biomedical prints that contact the human body, where brass is unsuitable
Better wear resistance than brass
Only $12.50
Cons:
Poor thermal conductivity (around a third of brass) — slower heat response and reduced maximum flow
Not suitable for regular CF/GF abrasive use — wears faster than hardened steel
May need +5°C on profiles vs brass
Name: V6 Stainless Steel
Description: Phaetus's stainless steel V6-style nozzle. Stainless steel is durable and corrosion-resistant, and because it is lead-free it is the right choice for food-level applications — prints for food processing, biomedical use, or anything that contacts the human body directly, where a brass nozzle is unsuitable. Standard M6 V6 thread. Available in 0.2, 0.4, 0.6 and 0.8mm. The trade-off is thermal conductivity well below brass, so expect slower heat response and slightly reduced maximum flow, and it is not a substitute for hardened steel under heavy abrasive use.
Verdict Label: Food-safe V6 nozzle for food and biomedical prints

Pros:
E3DLC diamond-like coating — significantly outperforms standard hardened steel
Reduces plastic adhesion and stringing at tip
Standard M6 thread — drop-in for any V6-compatible hotend
Available in fine sizes down to 0.25mm
Cons:
Premium price (~$32) vs clone hardened steel (~$3)
Max temp 300°C — not for ultra-high temp materials
Sometimes out of stock
Name: ObXidian V6
Description: E3D's ObXidian nozzles use an E3DLC (diamond-like carbon) coating that delivers exceptional wear resistance against abrasive filaments (CF, GF, metal fills). Community consensus puts ObXidian significantly ahead of standard hardened steel in wear life while maintaining better surface finish. The V6 model uses standard M6 thread and fits any V6-compatible hotend — Dragon, Rapido, Mosquito (with adapter), and others. Available in Revo-threaded variant as well.
Verdict Label: Best M6 abrasion-resistant nozzle for V6/Dragon/Rapido builds

Pros:
Standard M6 thread — drop-in for Rapido, Dragon, and any M6 hotend
Phaetus QC is generally solid
Available in hardened steel and ruby tip variants
Cons:
Not abrasive-safe (brass)
Rapido HF and UHF use Volcano-length nozzles, not standard M6 — confirm variant before ordering
No geometry advantages over other M6 nozzles
Name: Rapido Brass
Description: Standard M6 brass nozzle from Phaetus, sold as the replacement nozzle for their Rapido hotend series. The Rapido V1/V2 standard flow uses standard M6 length; the Rapido HF uses Volcano-length nozzles — confirm which Rapido variant you have before ordering. Standard M6 thread, no special bore geometry. For abrasive-safe printing on Rapido, CHT Hardened Steel or E3D ObXidian V6 (both standard M6) are the recommended upgrades.
Verdict Label: Standard nozzle for Rapido and Phaetus hotend ecosystem
